claim: A healthy adult woman with lifelong complete knockout of HAO1 was identified by sequencing autozygous human populations.
source: By sequencing autozygous human populations, we identified a healthy adult woman with lifelong complete knockout of HAO1 (expected ~1 in 30 million outbred people).
evidence: The manuscript describes the identification of this individual through exome sequencing of two population-based cohorts, with genetic confirmation via both exome sequencing and Sanger sequencing.

claim: Complete HAO1 knockout is expected in approximately 1 in 30 million outbred people.
source: By sequencing autozygous human populations, we identified a healthy adult woman with lifelong complete knockout of HAO1 (expected ~1 in 30 million outbred people).
evidence: This is an inference based on the cumulative frequency of pLOF variants in HAO1 from gnomAD v2.1 data showing approximately 1 in 2700 individuals is heterozygous.

claim: HAO1 (glycolate oxidase) silencing is the mechanism of lumasiran, an investigational RNA interference therapeutic for primary hyperoxaluria type 1.
source: HAO1 (glycolate oxidase) silencing is the mechanism of lumasiran, an investigational RNA interference therapeutic for primary hyperoxaluria type 1.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the therapeutic mechanism of lumasiran.

claim: The woman's plasma glycolate levels were 12 times the upper limit of normal observed in healthy reference individuals (n = 67).
source: Her plasma glycolate levels were 12 times, and urinary glycolate 6 times, the upper limit of normal observed in healthy reference individuals (n = 67).
evidence: Plasma glycolate was measured at 171 nmol/mL compared to reference range ≤14 nmol/mL, as shown in Table 1.

claim: The woman's urinary glycolate levels were 6 times the upper limit of normal observed in healthy reference individuals (n = 67).
source: Her plasma glycolate levels were 12 times, and urinary glycolate 6 times, the upper limit of normal observed in healthy reference individuals (n = 67).
evidence: Urine glycolate/creatinine ratio was measured at 199-309 mg/g compared to reference range ≤50 mg/g, as shown in Table 1.

claim: Plasma metabolomics and lipidomics analysis revealed 18 markedly elevated biochemicals (>5 sd outliers versus n = 25 controls).
source: Plasma metabolomics and lipidomics (1871 biochemicals) revealed 18 markedly elevated biochemicals (>5 sd outliers versus n = 25 controls) suggesting additional HAO1 effects.
evidence: This is based on analysis of 914 metabolites and 957 lipids from plasma samples compared to 25 control individuals.

claim: The woman has <2% residual glycolate oxidase activity based on comparison with lumasiran preclinical and clinical trial data.
source: Comparison with lumasiran preclinical and clinical trial data suggested she has <2% residual glycolate oxidase activity.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing her plasma and urinary glycolate levels to those observed in healthy volunteers receiving the highest dose of lumasiran (6 mg/Kg), which would be expected to silence HAO1 mRNA at >95%.

claim: Cell line expression of p.Leu333SerfsTer4 showed markedly reduced HAO1 protein levels.
source: Cell line p.Leu333SerfsTer4 expression showed markedly reduced HAO1 protein levels and cellular protein mis-localisation.
evidence: Western blot analysis (Figure 3A, 3B) demonstrated reduced HAO1 protein expression in cells transfected with the variant compared to wild-type.

claim: Cell line expression of p.Leu333SerfsTer4 showed cellular protein mis-localisation.
source: Cell line p.Leu333SerfsTer4 expression showed markedly reduced HAO1 protein levels and cellular protein mis-localisation.
evidence: Immunofluorescence microscopy (Figure 3D) showed diffuse distribution of the variant HAO1 protein within cells compared to the concentrated peroxisomal localization of wild-type.

claim: Lifelong HAO1 knockout in this woman is safe and without clinical phenotype.
source: In this woman, lifelong HAO1 knockout is safe and without clinical phenotype, de-risking a therapeutic approach and informing therapeutic mechanisms.
evidence: Medical history review and clinical assessments showed she was healthy with normal renal ultrasound, normal standard blood biochemistries, and normal plasma and urinary oxalate levels.

claim: The frameshift variant rs1186715161 (ENST00000378789.3:c.997delC, ENSP00000368066.3:p.Leu333SerfsTer4) is predicted to truncate the final 37 amino acids of the HAO1 protein.
source: The frameshift variant, rs1186715161 (present on a single Ensembl 99 transcript ENST00000378789.3:c.997delC, ENSP00000368066.3:p.Leu333SerfsTer4), for which the woman is homozygous, is predicted to truncate the final 37 amino acids of the HAO1 protein.
evidence: This is based on computational prediction of the effect of the frameshift variant on protein structure.

claim: The volunteer was 7.4% autozygous at the DNA level.
source: The volunteer was 7.4% autozygous at the DNA level and the genotype was within a long (5.2 Mb) autozygous region.
evidence: This is based on analysis of exome sequencing data to identify regions of homozygosity.

claim: The HAO1 knockout genotype was within a long (5.2 Mb) autozygous region.
source: The volunteer was 7.4% autozygous at the DNA level and the genotype was within a long (5.2 Mb) autozygous region.
evidence: This is based on analysis of exome sequencing data to identify regions of homozygosity.

claim: She was not homozygous for any other rare (minor allele frequency <1%) predicted loss-of-function genotypes.
source: She was not homozygous for any other rare (minor allele frequency <1%) predicted loss-of-function genotypes.
evidence: This is based on analysis of exome sequencing data.

claim: No complete knockout (homozygous predicted loss of function, pLOF) variants in HAO1 were observed in the gnomAD v2.1 database of 141,456 whole exome/genome sequenced individuals.
source: No complete knockout (homozygous predicted loss of function, pLOF) variants in HAO1 were observed in the online gnomAD v2.1 database of 141,456 whole exome/genome sequenced individuals (Karczewski, 2020; Minikel et al., 2019).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the gnomAD v2.1 database.

claim: The cumulative frequency of known pLOF variants in HAO1 is approximately 1 in 2700 individuals heterozygous in gnomAD v2.1.
source: The cumulative frequency of known pLOF variants in HAO1 is low, in gnomAD v2.1 approximately 1 in 2700 individuals is heterozygous.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the gnomAD v2.1 database.

claim: Analysis of pLOF constraint for HAO1 revealed 13 variants observed out of 17.7 expected (obs/exp = 74%, 90% CI 48–117%).
source: Analysis of pLOF constraint, to assess the degree of natural selection against loss of function, revealed 13 variants observed out of 17.7 expected (obs/exp = 74%, 90% CI 48–117%), with a confidence interval spanning the range for recessive disease genes (mean obs/exp = 59%) and homozygous pLoF tolerant genes (mean obs/exp = 92%) (Minikel et al., 2019).
evidence: This is based on constraint analysis using gnomAD data as described in Minikel et al., 2019.

claim: The HAO1 gene is unlikely to have a haploinsufficient phenotype based on lack of strong pLOF constraint.
source: The lack of strong constraint makes the HAO1 gene unlikely to have a haploinsufficient phenotype, but does not rule out a deleterious health effect in homozygotes or a mild phenotype in heterozygous carriers.
evidence: This is inferred from the pLOF constraint analysis showing obs/exp = 74% with confidence interval spanning both recessive disease genes and tolerant genes.

claim: Three children have previously been reported with suspected glycolate oxidase deficiency, however all were ascertained to have complicating factors.
source: Three children have previously been reported with suspected glycolate oxidase deficiency, however all were ascertained to have complicating factors such as multiple gene deletions or additional mutations associated with a severe genetic disease, thus confounding clinical interpretation. Furthermore none had plasma biochemical assays, and not all had HAO1 sequencing performed (Frishberg et al., 2014), (Clifford-Mobley et al., 2017), (Craigen, 1996).
evidence: This is based on review of previously published case reports.

claim: HAO1 inhibition is a potential chronic therapeutic approach for primary hyperoxaluria type 1 (PH1).
source: HAO1 inhibition is a potential chronic therapeutic approach for a devastating metabolic disease (primary hyperoxaluria type 1, PH1).
evidence: This is supported by the development of lumasiran and the therapeutic rationale described in the manuscript.

claim: At the time of assessment, the woman was in her 5th decade and a mother with three healthy children.
source: At the time of assessment, she was in her 5th decade and a mother with three healthy children.
evidence: This is based on medical history review.

claim: The woman declared British-Pakistani ethnicity.
source: She declared British-Pakistani ethnicity.
evidence: This is based on self-reported ethnicity.

claim: Renal ultrasound was normal.
source: Renal ultrasound, carried out as part of a gynaecology assessment, was normal.
evidence: This is based on clinical imaging assessment.

claim: The woman was overweight (BMI 30–35 kg/m2).
source: She was overweight (BMI 30–35 kg/m2), and other than common non-serious short-term illnesses and pregnancy symptoms, otherwise healthy.
evidence: This is based on clinical assessment.

claim: Standard clinical venous blood biochemistries including serum sodium, potassium, bicarbonate, chloride, creatinine, transaminases, and bilirubin were repeatedly normal at recall and over the previous decade.
source: Standard clinical venous blood biochemistries including serum sodium, potassium, bicarbonate, chloride, creatinine, transaminases, and bilirubin were repeatedly normal at recall and over the previous decade.
evidence: This is based on review of NHS health records and clinical assessments.

claim: At genotype directed recall, her serum anion gap was normal.
source: At genotype directed recall, her serum anion gap was normal, and plasma and urinary oxalate were both normal.
evidence: This is based on clinical biochemical testing.

claim: At genotype directed recall, plasma and urinary oxalate were both normal.
source: At genotype directed recall, her serum anion gap was normal, and plasma and urinary oxalate were both normal.
evidence: Plasma oxalate was <1.0 mcmol/L (reference <1.6) and urine oxalate/creatinine ratios were 20 and 23 mg/g (reference ≤75), as shown in Table 1.

claim: The majority of the woman's metabolites were similar (+/- 3 sd) compared to those of 25 control individuals.
source: Consistent with the expectation that HAO1 plays a relatively limited metabolic role, the majority of her metabolites were similar (+/- 3 sd) compared to those of 25 control individuals.
evidence: This is based on metabolomics analysis of 914 metabolites and 957 lipids.

claim: Principal component analysis of the metabolomics data showed the woman to be an outlier on PC2.
source: Principal component analysis of the metabolomics data showed her to be an outlier on PC2 (Figure 2), analysis of loadings suggested the high glycolate level to be the major driver.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2A where the red dots (HAO1 knockout replicates) are separated from black dots (controls) on PC2.

claim: Analysis of loadings suggested the high glycolate level to be the major driver of the PC2 outlier status.
source: Principal component analysis of the metabolomics data showed her to be an outlier on PC2 (Figure 2), analysis of loadings suggested the high glycolate level to be the major driver.
evidence: This is based on principal component analysis of metabolomics data.

claim: The elevated cholic acid related compounds might be due to reduced local availability of glycine to conjugate cholic acid and its bile acid derivatives.
source: The elevated cholic acid related compounds might be due to reduced local availability of glycine (a product of the glycolate pathway) to conjugate cholic acid and its bile acid derivatives (unconjugated bile acids are elevated; glycine and taurine conjugated bile acids are reduced).
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed metabolite changes based on known metabolic pathways.

claim: Unconjugated bile acids are elevated in the HAO1 knockout woman.
source: The elevated cholic acid related compounds might be due to reduced local availability of glycine (a product of the glycolate pathway) to conjugate cholic acid and its bile acid derivatives (unconjugated bile acids are elevated; glycine and taurine conjugated bile acids are reduced).
evidence: This is based on metabolomics data analysis.

claim: Glycine and taurine conjugated bile acids are reduced in the HAO1 knockout woman.
source: The elevated cholic acid related compounds might be due to reduced local availability of glycine (a product of the glycolate pathway) to conjugate cholic acid and its bile acid derivatives (unconjugated bile acids are elevated; glycine and taurine conjugated bile acids are reduced).
evidence: This is based on metabolomics data analysis.

claim: Six of the significantly elevated metabolites have a structure compatible with being potential HAO1 substrates.
source: Six of the significantly elevated metabolites have a structure compatible with being potential HAO1 substrates, two further evidenced by reduced levels of their predicted metabolic products (annotated in Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of elevated metabolites and knowledge of HAO1 substrate specificity.

claim: At the highest lumasiran dose tested (6 mg/Kg) in healthy volunteers, maximal plasma glycolate and urinary glycolate concentrations were 3–5 times less than observed in the HAO1 knockout woman.
source: In healthy volunteers at the highest dose tested (6 mg/Kg) maximal plasma glycolate and urinary glycolate concentrations were 3–5 times less than observed in the HAO1 knockout woman.
evidence: This is based on comparison of data from the HAO1 knockout woman with data from a phase one trial (32 individuals, https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT02706886).

claim: The lumasiran dose of 6 mg/Kg would be expected to silence the HAO1 mRNA at >95% based upon modeling from preclinical results and clinical data.
source: This lumasiran dose would be expected to silence the HAO1 mRNA at >95% based upon modeling from preclinical results in mice, rats, and monkeys and from direct comparison to clinical data from RNAi therapeutics to other targets that employ the same molecular design and have similar potency (Fitzgerald et al., 2017; Hill et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on modeling and comparison with other RNAi therapeutics as described in cited references.

claim: HAO1 protein is normally found exclusively in hepatocyte peroxisomes.
source: HAO1 protein is normally found exclusively in hepatocyte peroxisomes and requires the C-terminal tripeptide SKI for this targeting (Recalcati et al., 2001).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited reference.

claim: HAO1 requires the C-terminal tripeptide SKI for peroxisomal targeting.
source: HAO1 protein is normally found exclusively in hepatocyte peroxisomes and requires the C-terminal tripeptide SKI for this targeting (Recalcati et al., 2001).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited reference.

claim: The p.Leu333SerfsTer4 HAO1 protein is predicted to lack the entire C-terminus.
source: Since this woman's HAO1 protein is predicted to lack the entire C-terminus, we hypothesized an error in peroxisomal targeting might contribute to loss of function.
evidence: This is inferred from the frameshift variant truncating the final 37 amino acids, which would include the C-terminal targeting sequence.

claim: mRNA levels were unaffected by the p.Leu333SerfsTer4 variant in cell line assays.
source: Results with p.Leu333SerfsTer4 revealed markedly reduced HAO1 protein (mRNA levels were unaffected) with the p.Leu333SerfsTer4 HAO1 protein also diffusely distributed (mis-localised) within cells.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3C where mRNA expression levels are similar between wild-type and variant.

claim: PH1 is a rare autosomal recessive metabolic disorder of oxalate metabolism.
source: PH1 is a rare autosomal recessive metabolic disorder of oxalate metabolism (Cochat and Rumsby, 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited reference.

claim: Overproduction of oxalate in PH1 occurs in the liver due to an inherited genetic defect of the enzyme alanine-glyoxylate aminotransferase (encoded by AGXT).
source: Overproduction of oxalate occurs in the liver due to an inherited genetic defect of the enzyme alanine-glyoxylate aminotransferase (encoded by AGXT).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the pathophysiology of PH1.

claim: High concentrations of urinary oxalate in PH1 result in precipitation of insoluble calcium oxalate salts and may lead to paediatric end stage kidney disease.
source: High concentrations of urinary oxalate result in precipitation of insoluble calcium oxalate salts and may lead to paediatric end stage kidney disease.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the clinical consequences of PH1.

claim: Multi-organ damage can occur from systemic oxalosis in PH1.
source: Multi-organ damage can also occur from systemic oxalosis.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the clinical consequences of PH1.

claim: Substantial unmet need exists for therapies to treat PH1 without requiring dual liver-kidney transplantation.
source: Substantial unmet need exists for therapies to treat PH1 without requiring dual liver-kidney transplantation.
evidence: This is established knowledge about current treatment limitations for PH1.

claim: Glycolate oxidase is directly upstream of AGXT.
source: Glycolate oxidase is directly upstream of AGXT, reducing glycolate oxidase activity is expected to decrease oxalate production and increase glycolate levels.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the metabolic pathway.

claim: Reducing glycolate oxidase activity is expected to decrease oxalate production and increase glycolate levels.
source: Glycolate oxidase is directly upstream of AGXT, reducing glycolate oxidase activity is expected to decrease oxalate production and increase glycolate levels.
evidence: This is based on understanding of the metabolic pathway and supported by the observed phenotype in the HAO1 knockout woman.

claim: Excess glycolate is expected to be freely excreted by the kidneys and is highly soluble.
source: Excess glycolate is expected to be freely excreted by the kidneys and is highly soluble.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of glycolate biochemistry and supported by the normal renal function in the HAO1 knockout woman despite very high glycolate levels.

claim: Pre-clinical lumasiran studies in mice, rats, and monkeys suggested no adverse signals from chronic HAO1 silencing of >95%, with the expected substantial elevations in glycolate levels.
source: Pre-clinical lumasiran studies in mice, rats, and monkeys suggested no adverse signals from chronic HAO1 silencing of >95%, with the expected substantial elevations in glycolate levels (Liebow et al., 2017; Martin-Higueras et al., 2016; Dutta et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on preclinical studies cited in the references.

claim: HAO1 can metabolise 2-hydroxy fatty acids in addition to its glycolate oxidase activity.
source: For example, as well as its glycolate oxidase activity, HAO1 can also metabolise 2-hydroxy fatty acids.
evidence: This is established knowledge about HAO1 substrate specificity.

claim: PCSK9, LPA and APOC3 are classic examples of human knockouts providing drug target de-risking.
source: PCSK9, LPA and APOC3 are classic examples (Zhao et al., 2006), (Lim et al., 2014), (Saleheen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is based on previously published studies cited in the references.

claim: In selected populations where consanguineous unions are more common, the odds of homozygous mutations of all kinds increases profoundly due to autozygosity.
source: However, in selected populations where consanguineous unions are more common, the odds of homozygous mutations of all kinds increases profoundly due to autozygosity.
evidence: This is established knowledge about population genetics.

claim: The study of even a single human is equivalent to a typical knockout mouse study in terms of genetic background uniformity.
source: The study of even a single human is equivalent to a typical knockout mouse study, in that such mice are very highly inbred and near-identical, thus using multiple mice only increases measurement precision not the assessment of multiple genetic backgrounds.
evidence: This is a reasoning argument about the value of single human knockout studies.

claim: Exome sequencing was performed using Agilent in solution capture and Illumina short read sequencing.
source: Exome sequencing was performed using Agilent in solution capture and Illumina short read sequencing as described in detail in Narasimhan et al. (2016).
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study.

claim: The HAO1 variant rs1186715161 is present on a single transcript in Ensembl 99.
source: The HAO1 variant rs1186715161 is present on a single transcript in Ensembl 99 (which uses GENODE v33 BASIC); and on a single transcript in each of the GENCODE v32 comprehensive, NCBI RefSeq, CCDS (consensus coding sequence) annotations in the USCS genome browser.
evidence: This is based on bioinformatic annotation analysis.

source: Plasma oxalate	<1.0 mcmol/L	<1.6
evidence: This is shown in Table 1.

source: Plasma glycolate	171 nmol/mL	≤14
evidence: This is shown in Table 1.

claim: Plasma glycerate was <1 nmol/mL in the HAO1 knockout woman.
source: Plasma glycerate	<1 nmol/mL	≤28
evidence: This is shown in Table 1.

claim: Urine oxalate was 0.16 mmol/L in the HAO1 knockout woman (single void sample).
source: Urine oxalate	0.16 mmol/L	Not applicable
evidence: This is shown in Table 1.

source: Urine oxalate/creatinine ratio	20 mg/g	≤75
evidence: This is shown in Table 1.

claim: Urine glycolate/creatinine ratio was 199 mg/g in the HAO1 knockout woman (single void sample).
source: Urine glycolate/creatinine ratio	199 mg/g	≤50

claim: 24 hr urine oxalate was 0.27 mmol/24 hr in the HAO1 knockout woman.
source: Urine oxalate (total/24 hr)	0.27 mmol/24 hr	<0.46
evidence: This is shown in Table 1.

source: Urine oxalate/creatinine ratio	23 mg/g	≤75

claim: 24 hr urine glycolate/creatinine ratio was 309 mg/g in the HAO1 knockout woman.
source: Urine glycolate/creatinine ratio	309 mg/g	≤50

claim: The homozygous HAO1 knockout genotype was confirmed by inspection of blood DNA exome sequencing read data.
source: Inspection of blood DNA exome sequencing read data confirmed the genotype (Figure 1A), as did Sanger dideoxy sequencing in a further saliva DNA sample (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The homozygous HAO1 knockout genotype was confirmed by Sanger dideoxy sequencing in a saliva DNA sample.
source: Inspection of blood DNA exome sequencing read data confirmed the genotype (Figure 1A), as did Sanger dideoxy sequencing in a further saliva DNA sample (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Excellent correlation (r = 0.9976) between two duplicates of the HAO1 knockout samples was observed in metabolomics analysis.
source: Excellent correlation (r = 0.9976) between two duplicates of the HAO1 knockout samples were observed.
evidence: This is based on technical replicate analysis in the metabolomics assay.

claim: Excellent correlation (r = 0.9737) between two duplicates of the HAO1 knockout samples was observed in lipidomics analysis.
source: Excellent correlation (r = 0.9737) between two duplicates of the HAO1 knockout samples were observed.
evidence: This is based on technical replicate analysis in the lipidomics assay.

claim: The HD4 dataset comprises a total of 913 biochemicals, 735 compounds of known identity and 178 compounds of unknown structural identity.
source: The HD4 dataset comprises a total of 913 biochemicals, 735 compounds of known identity (named biochemicals) and 178 compounds of unknown structural identity (unnamed biochemicals).
evidence: This describes the metabolomics panel used.

claim: Analysis of glycolate was specifically added by Metabolon as an extra measurement to the standard 913 panel.
source: Analysis of glycolate (normally undetectable in this assay) was specifically added by Metabolon as an extra measurement to the standard 913 panel.
evidence: This describes a methodological detail of the metabolomics analysis.

claim: CHO-K1 cells were used for cell line expression assays.
source: Cell culture and transfection: CHO-K1 (ATCC CCL-61) were cultured in F-12K Medium supplemented with 10% FBS.
evidence: This describes the cell line used in the study.

claim: The cell line was authenticated using cytochrome C oxidase I gene (COI) analysis and confirmed mycoplasma free by ATCC.
source: This cell line was authenticated (cytochrome C oxidase I gene (COI) analysis) and confirmed mycoplasma free by the American Type Culture Collection (ATCC).
evidence: This describes quality control measures for the cell line.

claim: Data from the exome sequencing are available at the European Genome-phenome Archive under accession numbers EGAS00001000462, EGAS00001000511, EGAS00001000567, EGAS00001000717 and EGAS00001001301.
source: Data reported in the paper are available at the European Genotypephenome Archive (www.ebi.ac.uk/ega) under accession numbers EGAS00001000462, EGAS00001000511, EGAS00001000567, EGAS00001000717 and EGAS00001001301.
evidence: This describes data availability.
